feedback: Keep exchanges short and concrete for a 4-6 year old; follow the child's lead rather than quizzing.

If the child ties 'morning' or 'afternoon' to a particular activity rather than the time of day, gently re-anchor to the time of day itself — afternoon is the part of the day after the middle of the day (midday) until evening — and point out that several different activities can happen in the afternoon, so the label tracks the time, not one event.
Model correct use in the reply rather than correcting: if the child says 'yesterday' meaning tomorrow, respond with the concrete anchor ('oh, the park is tomorrow — the day that is coming!').
activities.intendedInsight: Time words are tools for talking about real, remembered and anticipated events — using them in authentic exchange is the goal, not reciting definitions.
learnerActions: Listen to a friendly character recount their own day in simple, concrete terms.
Tell the character what you did first and next in your own day.
Answer what you did yesterday and what you will do tomorrow, tied to real events you remember or expect.
Use 'morning' and 'afternoon' to say when something happened.
activities.title: Talk through your day with a character
